mainTopic: Carrying in stages through an אסקופה (threshold) and the dispute over אגד כלי, whether a container joins its contents
overview: This amud opens at the end of a proof that the measure for שבת is a כזית, based on the law of יוצא. The גמרא rejects the proof because the timing of the two cases is different. Next, אביי explains why the משנה needs to say that bringing an item back inside cancels its special status: the owner threw it into a storehouse, even though he still knows where it lies. A new משנה then teaches that someone who rests food on the אסקופה partway through carrying it out is פטור. It also teaches that a basket only partly carried out makes no one liable. The גמרא shows that the אסקופה must be a כרמלית, so the משנה disagrees with בן עזאי. חזקיה and רבי יוחנן then argue about אגד כלי, whether a container joins its contents into one unit. רבי זירא finds the משנה's wording hard for both views, and each אמורא resolves it his own way. Finally, חזקיה is defended against a ברייתא about a peddler's basket. רבי יוחנן is challenged from a case of stealing a purse on שבת, and that challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Proving the measure from consecrated meat that left the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove that the measure for שבת is a כזית. Its basis is that the measure for יוצא is a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: For יוצא, the measure is a כזית. So for שבת too, the measure should be a כזית!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of a proof that started on the previous page. The גמרא argues that since the measure for consecrated meat that left the עזרה (יוצא) is a כזית, the measure for שבת should also be a כזית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question being solved is what measure makes someone liable for carrying an item that is not normally fit to eat, such as impure תרומה. The proof compares this to קדשים that became פסול by leaving the courtyard, where a כזית is the important amount. If that comparison holds, שבת should follow the same כזית measure.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrated meat that left its permitted area (the עזרה) and became disqualified
An olive-bulk, a standard halachic measure

phrases.english: For 'leaving' (consecrated meat taken out), the measure is an olive-bulk,
phrases.notes: The sentence began on the previous page.

phrases.english: so with regard to Shabbat too, it should be an olive-bulk!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues an attempt, begun on the previous page, to settle the measure for שבת by comparison.
steps.raayaObject: That the שבת measure for this item is a כזית
steps.raayaSupportSource: The law of יוצא, where the significant measure is a כזית

steps.title: The comparison fails because the timing is different
steps.stepSummary: With יוצא, the disqualification happens before any שבת liability exists. In our case, שבת liability and טומאה happen at the same moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? There, as soon as he took it out past the courtyard wall, it became פסול as יוצא. But he is not liable for שבת until he brings it into the רשות הרבים. Here, שבת and טומאה come together at the same time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from יוצא. The two cases do not line up in time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With קדשים, the item becomes פסול the moment it passes the wall of the עזרה. Liability for שבת only begins later, when it reaches the רשות הרבים, so the two laws are separate events. In our case, the שבת violation and the טומאה happen at the same moment, so the measure that matters for טומאה also sets the measure for שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (a phrase that rejects a comparison)
The wall of the Temple courtyard

phrases.english: How can you compare?!
There, from the moment he took it outside the courtyard wall
it became disqualified because of 'leaving,'
but for Shabbat he is not liable
until he takes it out to the public domain,
here, Shabbat and impurity
come together at the same time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole comparison between יוצא and שבת
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: With יוצא, the disqualification and the שבת liability happen at different moments. In our case, they happen at the same time.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about bringing the item back in
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule: if he brought the item back in, he is only liable for a full standard measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If he went back and brought it in, he is only liable for its standard measure.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the earlier משנה. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that someone who stored seeds is liable for carrying even a tiny amount, because he showed the seeds matter to him. This line adds that once he brings the item back inside, a tiny amount is no longer enough, and he needs the normal שיעור to be liable.

keyTerms.meaning: He went back and brought it in

phrases.english: If he went back and brought it in,
he is only liable for its standard measure.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָזַר וְהִכְנִיסוֹ אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא כְּשִׁיעוּרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After bringing the item back in, liability requires the normal שיעור.

steps.title: Isn't this rule obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs to teach this rule at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה for teaching something that seems obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By bringing the item back in, the person shows he no longer treats it as special. So it seems clear that it should be judged like anyone else's item, with the normal measure. Why would the משנה bother to say so?

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious (a challenge that asks why a teaching is needed)

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges why the line quoted in step 3 is needed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Bringing the item back in plainly shows it has lost its special status, so there is no need to teach this.

steps.title: אביי: he threw it into a storehouse, and he knows where it landed
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains the case: he threw the item into a storehouse full of similar items, and he can still tell where it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: What case are we dealing with here? A case where he threw it into a storehouse, and he can still tell where it is.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the 'it's obvious' challenge. He narrows the משנה to a specific case where the rule is not obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a case of simply bringing the item home. He threw it into a pile of similar produce, yet he still knows exactly where his piece landed. That detail creates real doubt about whether the item is still special to him.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (narrows a teaching to a specific case)

phrases.english: Abaye said:
With what case are we dealing here?
For example, where he threw it into a storehouse
and its place can be recognized.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה refers to throwing the item into a storehouse while its place is still recognizable.

steps.title: Why the rule is needed: throwing it in cancels its status
steps.stepSummary: One might think the item stays special because he knows where it is. The משנה teaches that throwing it into the storehouse cancels its special status.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since he can still tell where it is, it keeps its first status. So the משנה teaches us that by throwing it into the storehouse, he cancelled that status.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his answer. He spells out the mistaken idea that the משנה comes to correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mistaken idea is that knowing the item's location means he still cares about it, so it stays special and a tiny amount would make him liable. The משנה teaches that the act of throwing it into a general storehouse is itself a cancellation, a ביטול. So a full שיעור is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken idea)

steps.whatToRemember: Throwing a stored item into a general storehouse cancels its special status, even if the owner knows where it lies. From then on, the normal שיעור applies.

phrases.english: You might have said:
since its place can be recognized,
it keeps its original status,
so it teaches us
that from the fact he threw it into the storehouse,
he has fully cancelled it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's answer by explaining what new point the משנה teaches.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the teaching is needed (מהו דתימא / קא משמע לן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because its place is recognizable, the item keeps its special status.
steps.terutzMaskana: Throwing it into the storehouse is a ביטול of its status.

steps.title: New משנה: carrying food out in two stages via the threshold
steps.stepSummary: Someone who rests food on the אסקופה and then takes it out further is פטור, because he did not do the מלאכה all at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone carries food out and puts it on the threshold. Whether he then carries it out further himself, or someone else carries it out, he is פטור, because he did not do his מלאכה all at once.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that carrying is only fully forbidden when it is done in one continuous act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking an item from one domain to another, הוצאה, makes a person liable only when it is done in one action. If the item first rests on the אסקופה, the action is split into two parts. Then neither he nor another person is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of the משנה)

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who carries out food
and placed it on the threshold,
whether he then carried it out further,
or another person carried it out, he is exempt,

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלֹּא עָשָׂה מְלַאכְתּוֹ בְּבַת אַחַת.
phrases.english: because he did not do his labor all at once.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Carrying out in two stages, with a rest on the threshold in between, is פטור.

steps.title: A basket that is only partly outside
steps.stepSummary: If a full basket is placed on the outer threshold, he is פטור even if most of the fruit is outside, until the whole basket is out.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he put a basket full of fruit on the outer threshold, even though most of the fruit is outside, he is פטור until he carries out the entire basket.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a second case. A basket placed partly outside does not make him liable until the whole basket is out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As long as part of the basket is still inside, he is פטור, even if most of the fruit is already outside. The משנה does not say whether this is because the basket joins the fruit into one unit or because each piece of fruit still sticks partly inside. חזקיה and רבי יוחנן argue about this in steps 15–16.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the majority, רוב, decides here. The basket must be fully out, even if most of the fruit is already outside.

phrases.english: A basket that is full of fruit
that he placed on the outer threshold,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁרוֹב פֵּירוֹת מִבַּחוּץ —
phrases.english: even though most of the fruit is outside,

phrases.aramaic: פָּטוּר, עַד שֶׁיּוֹצִיא אֶת כָּל הַקּוּפָּה.
phrases.english: he is exempt, until he carries out the entire basket.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second case in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no liability until the entire basket is out.

steps.title: What kind of domain is this threshold?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what legal status the אסקופה in the משנה has.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: This threshold, what is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking which domain the threshold belongs to. This sets up the attempts that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling of the משנה depends on whether the threshold is a רשות הרבים, a רשות היחיד, or something else. Each possibility will be checked against the משנה's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: The analysis section that follows the משנה
This one, what is it? (asks for the legal status)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
This threshold, what is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the analysis of the משנה in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The legal domain of the threshold

steps.title: If the threshold is a public domain, why is he exempt?
steps.stepSummary: If the threshold is a רשות הרבים, he already carried from a רשות היחיד into a רשות הרבים, so he should be חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the threshold is a רשות הרבים, why is he פטור? He carried from the רשות היחיד to the רשות הרבים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first option, that the threshold is a public domain, and shows it cannot work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the threshold is a רשות הרבים, then putting the food on it already finished a full act of carrying out. That should make him חייב. The משנה says פטור, so this option is rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces an option to be tested)

phrases.english: If you say it is a threshold with the status of the public domain,
why is he exempt?
But he carried out
from the private domain to the public domain!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to the question in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling of פטור, if the threshold is a רשות הרבים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Placing the food on the threshold would already complete הוצאה from a רשות היחיד to a רשות הרבים.

steps.title: Suggesting the threshold is a private domain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to a second option: the threshold is a רשות היחיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the threshold is a רשות היחיד.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first option failed, the גמרא tries the opposite one. This sets up the next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the threshold is private, then placing food on it does not finish any carrying out. That explains why the first stage is פטור. But the second stage still has to be checked.

phrases.english: Rather, it is a threshold with the status of the private domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second option after the first was rejected.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The threshold is a רשות היחיד.

steps.title: If it is private, the second stage should make him liable
steps.stepSummary: If the threshold is a רשות היחיד, then taking the food from it into the street is a full act of carrying out. So why is anyone פטור?
steps.simpleTranslation: Then why does the משנה say: 'Whether he carried it out himself or someone else carried it out, he is פטור'? He carried from the רשות היחיד to the רשות הרבים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the second option too. Under it, the second stage of carrying should make the person liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the threshold is private, moving the food from the threshold into the street is a full move from a רשות היחיד to a רשות הרבים. The first person, or the other person who carries it, should be חייב. Yet the משנה says פטור, so this option seems to fail as well.

keyTerms.meaning: That someone else carried them out

steps.whatToRemember: Both simple options fail. If the threshold is public, the first stage should make him liable. If it is private, the second stage should. This prepares the way for the גמרא to suggest a different kind of domain.

phrases.english: 'Whether he then carried it out further,
or another person carried it out, he is exempt'? Why?
But he carried out
from the private domain to the public domain!

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּין שֶׁחָזַר וְהוֹצִיאָן, בֵּין שֶׁהוֹצִיאָן אַחֵר — פָּטוּר? הָא קָא מַפֵּיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the option offered in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the threshold is a רשות היחיד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Moving the food from a private threshold into the street is a full act of הוצאה, so someone should be חייב.

steps.title: The threshold is a כרמלית
steps.stepSummary: After rejecting רשות הרבים and רשות היחיד, the גמרא concludes the threshold is a כרמלית. The משנה teaches that he is פטור only because the object came to rest there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the threshold is a כרמלית. The משנה is teaching us this: he is exempt only because the object came to rest in a כרמלית. If it did not rest in the כרמלית and only passed through it, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer to 'what kind of place is this threshold?' It is a כרמלית, a middle zone that the Rabbis treat strictly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying from a רשות היחיד into a כרמלית is not a Torah-level act of carrying out, so he is פטור. The new lesson comes from the reverse case. If the object only passes through the כרמלית on its way to the רשות הרבים without stopping, he is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: An in-between zone, neither fully private nor fully public, restricted by the Rabbis
This is what it teaches us

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that simply passing through a כרמלית makes him פטור. He is פטור only when the object actually comes to rest there.

phrases.english: Rather, the threshold is a karmelit,
and this is what it teaches us:
the reason he is exempt is that it rested in a karmelit,
but if it did not rest in a karmelit, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge in step 12 by choosing a third option for the threshold's status.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (a third category of domain)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The threshold had to be either a רשות הרבים or a רשות היחיד, and each option caused a problem.
steps.terutzMaskana: The threshold is a כרמלית. Resting there exempts him, but merely passing through does not.

steps.title: The משנה does not follow בן עזאי
steps.stepSummary: Because passing through a כרמלית still makes one חייב, the משנה disagrees with בן עזאי. בן עזאי exempts someone who carries from a store to a plaza by way of a colonnade.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה does not follow בן עזאי. A ברייתא teaches: one who carries from a store to a plaza by way of a colonnade is liable, and בן עזאי exempts him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the previous step. It identifies which side of a known מחלוקת our משנה follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The store is a רשות היחיד, the plaza is a רשות הרבים, and the colonnade in between is a כרמלית. The תנא קמא says the in-between zone does not interrupt the carrying, so he is חייב. בן עזאי holds that the middle zone interrupts the carrying. Our משנה implies he is חייב when the object only passes through, so it sides against בן עזאי.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who holds that carrying through an in-between zone interrupts the act
As it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: The threshold is a כרמלית. Carrying through a כרמלית without stopping still makes one חייב, which goes against בן עזאי.

phrases.english: Our mishna is not in accordance with Ben Azzai.
As it was taught: one who carries out from a store to a plaza
by way of a colonnade is liable,
and Ben Azzai exempts him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a consequence from step 13 and identifies the משנה's position in a known מחלוקת.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה follows the view that passing through a כרמלית does not interrupt carrying, which is against בן עזאי.

steps.title: חזקיה limits the basket rule to long produce
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה says the 'full basket' rule applies only to cucumbers and gourds. With mustard seeds he would be חייב, because the basket does not join its contents into one unit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'a basket that is full.' חזקיה said: this was taught only about a basket full of cucumbers and gourds. If it is full of mustard seeds, he is liable. So he holds that being held together in a vessel does not count as being joined.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the full-basket case from the משנה (step 8). חזקיה explains when that rule applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Long cucumbers and gourds each stick partly inside, so no single fruit has fully left. Small mustard seeds can lie fully outside on their own. חזקיה holds he is חייב for those seeds, which shows he thinks the basket does not unite its contents (אגד כלי לא שמיה אגד).

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who argues with רבי יוחנן here
They taught this only in the case of
Being bound together by a vessel

phrases.english: 'A basket that is full,' etc.
Chizkiyah said: they taught this only
regarding a basket full of cucumbers and gourds,
but if it is full of mustard seeds, he is liable.

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא קָסָבַר אֶגֶד כְּלִי — לָא שְׁמֵיהּ אֶגֶד.
phrases.english: Apparently he holds that binding by a vessel is not considered binding.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the full-basket clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The exemption applies only to long produce. Mustard seeds that are outside make him חייב, because אגד כלי לא שמיה אגד.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן exempts even mustard seeds
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says he is פטור even when the basket is full of mustard seeds, because the basket joins its contents into one unit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: even if the basket is full of mustard seeds, he is exempt. So he holds that being held together in a vessel does count as being joined.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the opposite view to חזקיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, the basket turns all its contents into one unit. Since part of the basket is still inside, every seed counts as still partly inside, so he is פטור. This is אגד כלי שמיה אגד.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who argues with חזקיה

steps.whyThisMatters: The disagreement over אגד כלי, whether a vessel turns its contents into one unit, drives the rest of this סוגיא.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
even if it is full of mustard seeds, he is exempt.

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא קָסָבַר אֶגֶד כְּלִי — שְׁמֵיהּ אֶגֶד.
phrases.english: Apparently he holds that binding by a vessel is considered binding.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ מְלֵיאָה חַרְדָּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to חזקיה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He is פטור even with mustard seeds, because אגד כלי שמיה אגד.

steps.title: רבי זירא: the משנה's wording fits neither view
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא claims that the precise wording of the משנה does not fit חזקיה and does not fit רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: a careful reading of the משנה does not fit חזקיה, and a careful reading does not fit רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רבי זירא announces a problem for both opinions, and the next two steps show the details.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each half of the משנה's wording will turn out to support one side. So each אמורא is contradicted by one half of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who examines the wording of the משנה
It reads precisely (as a careful inference from the wording)

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
the precise wording of our mishna is not like Chizkiyah,
and the precise wording is not like Rabbi Yochanan:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּחִזְקִיָּה דַּיְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges both opinions from steps 15 and 16.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Inferences from the משנה's exact words go against each opinion.

steps.title: The end of the משנה goes against חזקיה
steps.stepSummary: The words 'until he carries out the whole basket' imply that even when all the fruit is out, he is פטור as long as part of the basket is inside. That means אגד כלי שמיה אגד, which goes against חזקיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It does not fit חזקיה, because the משנה says 'until he carries out the whole basket.' The reason he is liable is that the whole basket went out. If only all the fruit went out, he is exempt. So the משנה holds that binding by a vessel counts as binding.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא explains the problem for חזקיה, using the last words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If liability depends on the whole basket going out, then fruit that is entirely outside still does not count while the basket is partly inside. That only makes sense if the basket joins the fruit into one unit, which חזקיה rejects.

keyTerms.meaning: Until he carries out the entire basket

phrases.english: It does not read precisely like Chizkiyah,
for it teaches: 'until he carries out the entire basket.'
The reason he is liable is the entire basket,
but if only all the fruit went out, he is exempt.

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא קָסָבַר אֶגֶד כְּלִי שְׁמֵיהּ אֶגֶד.
phrases.english: Apparently it holds that binding by a vessel is considered binding.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first half of רבי זירא's claim.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The phrase 'until he carries out the whole basket' implies אגד כלי שמיה אגד, the opposite of חזקיה's view.

steps.title: The middle of the משנה goes against רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The words 'even though most of the fruit is outside' imply that if all the fruit were outside he would be חייב. That means אגד כלי לא שמיה אגד, which goes against רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It does not fit רבי יוחנן, because the משנה says 'even though most of the fruit is outside.' The reason he is exempt is that only most of the fruit is out. If all the fruit were out, he would be liable, even though the basket holds it together from inside. So the משנה holds that binding by a vessel does not count as binding.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא explains the problem for רבי יוחנן, using the earlier words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stresses 'most,' which suggests that 'all' would change the outcome. If all the fruit outside makes him חייב even while the basket is still inside, then the basket does not join the fruit into one unit. That is the opposite of רבי יוחנן's view.
steps.confusionAlert: Notice the clash: the משנה's middle phrase points to 'not joined,' but its last phrase points to 'joined.' That clash sets up the next step.

phrases.english: It does not read precisely like Rabbi Yochanan,

phrases.aramaic: דְּקָתָנֵי: ״אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁרוֹב פֵּירוֹת בַּחוּץ״ —
phrases.english: for it teaches: 'even though most of the fruit is outside.'
The reason he is exempt is that only most of the fruit is out,
but if all the fruit is out,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דַּאֲגִידָא קוּפָּה מִגַּוַּאי — חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: even though the basket is bound inside, he is liable.

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא קָסָבַר אֶגֶד כְּלִי לָא שְׁמֵיהּ אֶגֶד.
phrases.english: Apparently it holds that binding by a vessel is not considered binding.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the second half of רבי זירא's claim.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The phrase 'even though most of the fruit is outside' implies that all the fruit outside would make him חייב, which means אגד כלי לא שמיה אגד.

steps.title: The two inferences contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the משנה now seems to contradict itself, so it must be resolved somehow.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then it is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that רבי זירא's two inferences clash within the same משנה. It sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One phrase implies the basket joins the fruit, and the other implies it does not. A single משנה cannot hold both. So the משנה itself needs to be explained.

phrases.english: But then it is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out that the inferences in steps 18 and 19 contradict each other.
steps.kashyaTarget: The internal consistency of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two inferences from the same משנה lead to opposite rules about אגד כלי.

steps.title: Each אמורא resolves the משנה his own way
steps.stepSummary: Both חזקיה and רבי יוחנן can explain the משנה according to their own reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה explains the משנה according to his view, and רבי יוחנן explains it according to his view.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. It announces that each side has a reading of the משנה, and the next two steps show how each one works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither opinion is refuted. Each אמורא reads one phrase literally and explains the other phrase so that it fits his view.

keyTerms.meaning: Resolves it according to his own reasoning

phrases.english: Chizkiyah resolves it according to his reasoning,
and Rabbi Yochanan resolves it according to his reasoning.

steps.triggerLanguage: חִזְקִיָּה מְתָרֵץ לְטַעְמֵיהּ, וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מְתָרֵץ לְטַעְמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the contradiction from step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to contradict itself and both opinions.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each אמורא has a consistent reading of the משנה.

steps.title: חזקיה's reading: the whole-basket rule is only for long produce
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה says 'until he carries out the whole basket' refers only to cucumbers and gourds. With mustard seeds, having the seeds outside counts like taking out the whole basket, so he is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה explains it his way. 'Until he carries out the whole basket': when is this said? With a basket full of cucumbers and gourds. But if it is full of mustard seeds, he is treated as though he carried out the whole basket, and he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה explains away the phrase that went against him (step 18).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'whole basket' only seemed to say the basket joins the fruit. חזקיה says it simply describes long produce, where no single fruit is fully out until the whole basket is. With mustard seeds, the seeds outside count by themselves, so he is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case are these words said?
He is treated as one who carried out

phrases.english: Chizkiyah resolves it according to his reasoning:
'until he carries out the entire basket':
in what case is this said?
With a basket full of cucumbers and gourds,
but if it is full of mustard seeds,

phrases.aramaic: נַעֲשֶׂה כְּמִי שֶׁהוֹצִיא אֶת כָּל הַקּוּפָּה, וְחַיָּיב.
phrases.english: he is treated as one who carried out the entire basket, and he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out חזקיה's resolution announced in step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting a phrase to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Whole basket' meant the basket joins its contents (אגד כלי שמיה אגד).
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Whole basket' applies only to long produce. With mustard seeds he is חייב.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's reading: even all the fruit outside is exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reads 'even though most of the fruit is outside' as 'not only most, but even all.' He is פטור until the whole basket is out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן explains it his way. 'Even though most of the fruit is outside' means not only most of the fruit, but even all the fruit, he is still exempt, until he carries out the whole basket.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains away the phrase that went against him (step 19), and this resolves the סוגיא's contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'most' is not a precise limit. It is a 'not only this, but even that' style of speech. So even with all the fruit outside, the basket still joins it to the inside, and he is פטור. This matches אגד כלי שמיה אגד.
steps.whatToRemember: חזקיה holds אגד כלי לא שמיה אגד and limits the 'whole basket' rule to long produce. רבי יוחנן holds אגד כלי שמיה אגד and reads 'most' as 'even all.' Each can explain the משנה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan resolves it according to his reasoning:
'even though most of the fruit is outside'
and not only most of the fruit,
but even all the fruit, he is exempt,
until he carries out the entire basket.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out רבי יוחנן's resolution announced in step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the wording as 'not only this, but even that'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Most' implied that 'all' would make him חייב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even with all the fruit outside he is פטור until the whole basket leaves.

steps.title: The peddler's basket challenges חזקיה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that someone who carries a peddler's basket to the outer threshold is פטור even though most of the items are outside. If the basket holds bundles, this is hard for חזקיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: One who carries out a peddler's basket and puts it on the outer threshold is exempt, even though most of the kinds of items are outside, until he carries out the whole basket. You might think the basket holds bundles. If so, this is difficult for חזקיה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to attack חזקיה. In that case, most of the items in the basket are outside, and yet the carrier is פטור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיה holds that a container does not 'bind' its contents (אגד כלי לא שמיה אגד). On his view, items that are fully outside count as carried out even if the basket is not. If the basket is full of separate bundles, many bundles are completely outside, so חזקיה should say חייב, but the ברייתא says פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from an authoritative source)
A peddler's basket holding many kinds of goods, mostly spices
The outer threshold (here treated as the outside area)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One who carries out the peddler's basket
and placed it on the outer threshold,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁרוֹב מִינִין בַּחוּץ
phrases.english: even though most of the kinds of items are outside

phrases.aramaic: — פָּטוּר, עַד שֶׁיּוֹצִיא אֶת כָּל הַקּוּפָּה.
phrases.english: he is exempt, until he carries out the entire basket.
You might think it refers to bundles,
phrases.notes: Each bundle is a separate unit, so some are completely outside.

phrases.english: so it is difficult for Chizkiya!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both חזקיה and רבי יוחנן explained the משנה their own way, the גמרא now tests חזקיה against a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: חזקיה's view that אגד כלי לא שמיה אגד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the basket holds separate bundles, many are fully outside. By חזקיה he should be חייב, yet the ברייתא rules פטור.

steps.title: חזקיה answers: the basket holds long stalks
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה answers that the ברייתא deals with long stalks that run the whole length of the basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה can say to you: What case are we dealing with here? With long stalks.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה defends himself by saying the basket in the ברייתא holds long stalks, not separate bundles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Long stalks stretch from one end of the basket to the other. As long as part of the basket is still inside, part of every stalk is still inside, so no item is fully outside. That is why he is פטור, even according to חזקיה.

keyTerms.meaning: He can say to you (a defense given on someone's behalf)
What case are we dealing with here? (narrows the case)
Long stalks that fill the whole length of the basket

phrases.english: Chizkiya can say to you:
With what are we dealing here?
With long stalks.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ חִזְקִיָּה הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24 by changing what the basket contains.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the basket held separate bundles, some of them completely outside.
steps.terutzMaskana: The basket holds long stalks, so part of each item is still inside. The item is not fully out, and חזקיה agrees he is פטור.

steps.title: רב ביבי brings the case of stealing a purse on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי בר אביי quotes a source: a thief who lifts a purse on שבת must pay, but one who drags it out does not pay, because the theft and the שבת violation happen at the same moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי בר אביי challenged: One who steals a purse on שבת is liable to pay, because he already became liable for theft before he reached the שבת prohibition. If he was dragging it out, he is exempt, because the theft prohibition and the שבת prohibition come at the same time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge, this time against רבי יוחנן. First it quotes the source about the stolen purse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When one act earns both a death penalty (שבת) and a money payment (theft), only the harsher punishment applies (קים ליה בדרבה מיניה). If he lifts the purse, the theft is complete right away, before he carries it outside, so he must pay. If he drags it, the theft is only complete when it leaves the owner's domain, which is the same moment he breaks שבת, so he does not pay.

keyTerms.meaning: He receives only the harsher of two punishments (background rule)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Liable' and 'exempt' here are about paying for the theft, not about the שבת punishment. If the theft and the שבת violation happen together, the harsher שבת penalty cancels the payment.

phrases.english: Rav Beivai bar Abaye raised an objection:
One who steals a purse on Shabbat is liable,
because he was already liable for theft
before he came to the Shabbat prohibition.
phrases.notes: Lifting the purse completes the theft before he carries it out.

phrases.english: If he was dragging it out, he is exempt,
since the prohibition of theft and the prohibition of Shabbat
come at the same time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending חזקיה, the גמרא turns to a source that will challenge רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that אגד כלי שמיה אגד (the attack itself comes in the next step)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This step lays down the source. The next step shows how it clashes with רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: If a container binds its contents, the theft should come first
steps.stepSummary: If אגד כלי שמיה אגד, then even when he drags the purse, the theft is complete before the שבת violation, so he should have to pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think the binding of a vessel counts as binding, then the theft prohibition comes before the שבת prohibition!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now uses the purse case to attack רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If אגד כלי שמיה אגד, then for שבת he is only חייב once the whole purse is out. For theft, though, the money counts as taken once the mouth of the purse is outside, since he can reach the coins. So the theft happens first and he should pay, but the source says the dragger is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: A container's binding counts: items inside are treated as one unit with the container

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that the binding of a vessel is considered binding,
then the prohibition of theft comes first
before the prohibition of Shabbat!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ אֶגֶד כְּלִי שְׁמֵיהּ אֶגֶד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב ביבי's challenge by applying the source to רבי יוחנן's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן: אגד כלי שמיה אגד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבי יוחנן, the שבת violation waits until the whole purse is out, but the theft is complete once the mouth is out. The theft comes first, so the dragger should pay, which contradicts the source.

steps.title: The purse was dragged out bottom-first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that if the mouth came out first, the theft would come first. The source, however, deals with a purse dragged out bottom-first.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he took it out mouth-first, yes, that is true. But what case are we dealing with here? Where he took it out bottom-first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן by limiting the source to a purse dragged out by its bottom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the bottom comes out first, the thief cannot reach the money until the whole purse is outside. So the theft and the שבת violation finish at the same moment, and he is פטור from paying even if אגד כלי שמיה אגד.

keyTerms.meaning: By way of its mouth (opening first)
By way of its bottom (base first)

phrases.english: If he took it out by way of its mouth
indeed, that is so.
With what are we dealing here?
Where he took it out by way of its bottom.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי דְּאַפְּקֵיהּ דֶּרֶךְ פִּיו הָכִי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ביבי's challenge in step 27.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The purse was dragged out in a way that the money became reachable before the whole purse was outside.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was dragged out bottom-first, so the money is reachable only when the whole purse is out. Theft and שבת come together, which fits רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: But the seam could still give access
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to challenge the bottom-first answer: there is still the area of the seam.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is still the area of the seam.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. Even with the bottom out first, the seam may let the thief reach the money early. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bottom-first answer works only if no money can be reached until the whole purse is out. The גמרא suggests the seam area could let him get at the coins sooner, which would make the theft come first again.

keyTerms.meaning: The area of the seam, where the purse is stitched together

phrases.english: But isn't there the area of the seam,
phrases.notes: The challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the bottom-first answer given in step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the purse was dragged out bottom-first
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even bottom-first, the seam may let the thief reach the money before the whole purse is out, so the theft would still come before the שבת violation.
